read: full: abstract, sections 1-6, appendix A (legal compliance), A.1 (Table 2), A.4-A.6; the A.2-A.3 metric tables and example responses and the A.7 prompts skimmed
venue_now: ICML 2025, PMLR 267 (p1 footer); arXiv 2508.08292v2, 27 Aug 2025. The May entry cites the version at the 4th MATH-AI Workshop at NeurIPS'24; the text read here is the later ICML version, whose title ends 'in LLMs' and which has an eighth author (Elyas Obbad).
what_it_is: Putnam-AXIOM Original is 522 problems from the William Lowell Putnam Competition (1938-2023) in 11 domains, chosen for a unique, automatically checkable final answer; 221 of them (42.3%) were altered by adding a step so that they end in one boxed answer (p4). Putnam-AXIOM Variation adds Python scripts for 100 of the problems that change variable names, constants and phrasing, generating unlimited new instances (p1-2, p4-5). Models are scored on boxed answers with a SymPy-based equivalence function (p2, p26), complemented by Teacher-Forced Accuracy (TFA), the share of reference-solution tokens a model predicts correctly under teacher forcing (p6).
domain: undergraduate competition mathematics, 11 domains: geometry, algebra, trigonometry, calculus, linear algebra, combinatorics, probability, number theory, complex numbers, differential equations, analysis (p4)
size: 522 Original problems; Variation scripts for 100 problems (37 constant-plus-variable changes, 63 variable-only), each evaluated over five generated snapshots (p4-5); 18 models in Table 1 (p7) and 21 in Table 2 (p14)
source_of_items: competitions (Putnam), with modified boxing (p4); variants perturbed programmatically from the originals (p4-5)
instances: static (Original) and perturbed/generated (Variation: 'an unlimited stream of equally difficult, unseen instances', p1)
has_gold_traces: yes: each problem keeps its full written solution, standardised with the boxed answer moved to the end (p13); the variation scripts also change the constants inside the step-by-step solution (p4); TFA is computed on these reference solutions (p6)
evaluation: final answer (boxed answer, SymPy-based equivalence, p2, p26) plus Teacher-Forced Accuracy, a reference-likelihood proxy computed from the model's next-token predictions on the gold solution, not a check of the model's own generated steps; it needs log-probabilities, so proprietary models have no TFA (p6-7, Table 1)
human_validation: None reported for the items, the modified boxing or the variants; there is a qualitative error analysis of model responses (p7-8, appendix A.3). TFA is validated only by its correlation with boxed accuracy, on MATH across 15 open models (p7) and on Putnam-AXIOM (correlation 0.52, p9); comparing TFA with expert grading is listed as future work (p9).
contamination_measures: perturbations: functional variants of 100 problems (p2, p4); a fine-tuning experiment simulating contamination raised accuracy on the originals from 23% to 80% but on the variants only from 12% to 33% (p5)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-M1 (L155-161): '... benchmarks ranging from GSM8K ... and Math ... to HardMath ..., Putnam-Axiom (Gulati et al., 2024), and GSM-Symbolic ... rigorously test abstract logical deduction and reasoning stability.'
engtrace_use.explanation: The gist fits better than for the other mathematics entries: Putnam problems are advanced, abstract mathematics (p1, p4), the paper calls itself 'rigorous' (p1), and the Variation set measures accuracy drops under perturbation (p7-8), which the authors read as memorisation or contamination (p1, p9) rather than as 'stability'. But the benchmark scores boxed final answers and altered 42.3% of its problems to obtain one (p4), so it does not test deduction (proofs) directly. The sentence also omits the two features that bear on EngTrace: the Variation scripts generate unlimited instances with matching solutions (p1-2, p4), a precedent for EngTrace's generated instances that S-I2 does not credit; and TFA, a step-level metric the authors position against process reward models (p4-5), which qualifies any claim that prior benchmarks score only outcomes.

suggested_wording: Putnam-AXIOM (Gulati et al., 2025) pairs 522 Putnam problems with scripted functional variants of 100 of them, on which most models score lower than on the originals, and complements boxed-answer accuracy with teacher-forced accuracy on the reference solution.
facts_to_cite: 522 problems from the William Lowell Putnam Competition, 1938-2023, in 11 domains, chosen for a unique final answer that can be checked automatically (p4).
221 of the 522 problems (42.3%) were modified by adding a step so that they end in a single boxed answer (p4).

Functional variants exist for 100 problems: Python scripts change variable names, constants and phrasing (37 constant-plus-variable, 63 variable-only) and can generate unlimited new instances (p2, p4-5).

18 of the 21 models in Table 2 score lower on the variants than on the corresponding originals (counted from Table 2, p14); in a simulated-contamination fine-tuning experiment, accuracy on the originals rose from 23% to 80% and on the variants from 12% to 33% (p5).
Boxed answers are compared with the ground truth by a SymPy-based equivalence function (p2, p26).

Teacher-Forced Accuracy is the fraction of reference-solution tokens predicted correctly under teacher forcing (p6); the authors present it as a lightweight alternative to process reward models (p4-5) and leave its comparison with expert grading to future work (p9).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: programmatic generation of new instances from source problems, with the constants changed in the step-by-step solution too (p4), and a contamination rationale for it (p1-2, p5); reference solutions for every item; an explicit aim to go beyond final answers (TFA, p5). Lacks: engineering domain; step-level verification of the model's own trace (TFA scores how well a model predicts the gold solution, and penalises valid alternative paths, p9); expert validation of items or evaluator (none); a private pool (generation code public, p1); variants cover only 100 of the 522 problems (p9).
notes: Confidence is high on the facts; medium on imprecise rather than accurate. Version: the revision should cite the ICML 2025 version (Gulati et al., 2025, eight authors, title ending 'in LLMs'), since that is the version read here; the workshop version could not be checked. Internal inconsistencies, so the revision should not quote drop sizes: the abstract gives o1-preview a 19.6-point drop (46.8% relative) from 41.9% (p1), the text says 'o1-preview at 17%' (p7), and Table 2 shows 51/100 on the originals and 43/100 on the variants (p14); the abstract's 'remaining eighteen models' (p1) does not match the 21 models in Table 2; appendix A.4 still refers to 262 Original and 60 Variation questions (p24). Together with HARDMath, it is a generated-instance precedent that S-I2 does not credit (S-I2 credits only GSM-Symbolic and FinChain).
